title: Miniwave Patch: Synapse deploy cadence and watchlist
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational sketch for the March miniwave patch to the Synapse service. Goal is to push a small code + config change (KV cache tuning, two runtime flags) with minimal blast radius, verify telemetry, and land in prod with a rapid rollback plan. Intended for weekday mid-window (non-peak) and a thin ops crew (on-call + release lead).

High-level objectives:
- Push patch that reduces tail latency for long-context requests by adjusting adaptive-batch thresholds.
- Validate correctness with end-to-end smoke tests and sampling traces.
- Keep cost/latency SLOs stable; avoid capacity churn by enabling gradual canary.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In: synapse service binary bump (v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4), runtime flag: enable-adaptive-batch=true, kv-cache-size +10%, config rollout.
- Out: any schema migrations, data-store changes, infra reboots. If a migration is discovered, revert to staging.

Quick owners and contacts:
- Release lead: Ava Martinez (pager + slack)
- On-call infra: Liam Chen (pager)
- SRE telemetry lead: Priya Nair (slack)
- QA smoke: Diego Alvarez (email)

7-day deployment calendar (compact):
Mon 2026-03-15: staging validation, long-run load test (12h), finalize runbook.
Tue 2026-03-16: create canary job artifacts, deploy to canary pool (1 node, 0.5% traffic), basic smoke checks.
Wed 2026-03-17: expand canary to 5% (5 nodes), run replays, check top-10 customer paths.
Thu 2026-03-18: extend canary to 20% if green; begin gradual ramp plan.
Fri 2026-03-19: full rollout window (scheduled mid-day low-traffic window), monitor until EOD.
Sat 2026-03-20: quiet day; on-call monitoring; revert if anomalies.
Sun 2026-03-21: closeout notes and metrics digest.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any prod action):
- [ ] Branch built and smoke-tested in CI (artifact exists: synapse-1.12.4.tar.gz).
- [ ] Staging run: 12h load test with 99th latency < 2x baseline.
- [ ] Canary config prepared (k8s deployment manifest + traffic split).
- [ ] Rollback image verified (previous prod tag synapse-1.12.3).
- [ ] Pager duty / on-call roster confirmed for window.
- [ ] Slack #release channel created and pinned runbook.
- [ ] Telemetry queries (below) copy-pasted to dash.
- [ ] Smoke tests on critical routes (auth, caching, backpressure) passing.

Canary schedule and thresholds (operational):
- Step 0: 0.5% (1 replica) — quick smoke (5m) and trace sampling. Abort if error rate > 0.5% above baseline or 99p latency > 1.5x.
- Step 1: 5% (5 replicas) — 30m steady-state. Abort if error rate trend upwards or P95 increases > 20%.
- Step 2: 20% (20 replicas) — 1h steady-state, run replay suite and customer path checks. Abort if sustained failure or elevated resource usage (CPU/GPU > 80%).
- Step 3: progressive ramp to 100% over 2 hours with telemetry gating.

Immediate abort signals (examples):
- Error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 10 minutes.
- Latency P99 > 3x baseline for any 5m window.
- OOMs/restarts observed in canary pods.
- Traffic shift causes downstream queue length to increase > 2x for 10m.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
1) Trigger k8s rollout undo: kubectl rollout undo deployment/synapse -n prod --to-revision=<prev-rev>
2) If undo fails, scale down new deployment and scale up prod revision replicas: kubectl scale deployment/synapse-new --replicas=0; kubectl scale deployment/synapse-old --replicas=<target>
3) Revert config flags in redis/kvs via admin console (flag: enable-adaptive-batch=false).
4) Notify #release (template below) and open incident page.

Telemetry queries (copy into observability dashboard):
- Error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="synapse",status!~"2.."}[1m])) by (cluster) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="synapse"}[1m]))
- P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="synapse"}[5m])) by (le))
- Pod restarts: sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{pod=~"synapse.*"}[10m]))
- Downstream queue length: max_over_time(queue_length{service="kvs"}[10m])

Runbook quick commands:
- Check canary pods: kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=synapse-canary -o wide
- Dump pod logs (since start): kubectl logs -n prod synapse-canary-<pod> --since=60m
- Force rollback (one-liner): kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/synapse && kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/synapse --timeout=10m

Slack templates:
- Start: ":rocket: Starting Synapse miniwave patch (v1.12.4) — canary 0.5% now. Release lead: @ava"
- Green progress: ":white_check_mark: Canary @ 5% stable for 30m. Proceeding to 20% per plan."
- Abort/rollback: ":warning: Abort: error rate spike observed at canary 20%. Initiating rollback to v1.12.3. See incident doc: <link>"

Draft release notes (short):
Title: Synapse v1.12.4 — adaptive batch tuning
Summary: Adjusted adaptive-batching thresholds and modest KV cache increase to improve tail latency on long-context requests. No schema changes.
Notable changes:
- Runtime flag enable-adaptive-batch=true (default off in previous release).
- KV cache increased by 10% to reduce remote reads for long sequences.
- Minor dependency bump to downstream router to address small header bug.
Impact: Lower P95/P99 for long-context flows; expected neutral cost impact.
Rollout: Canary -> ramp -> full. See observability notes for gating thresholds.

Open questions / notes to self:
- We saw a small transient in staging at ~8h during load test; need to confirm if it's repro on older image (replay time alignment).
- Double-check that downstream router header change is backwards compatible for older clients.
- Consider adding a short synthetic test that hits 2-min context windows specifically.

Post-release checklist (after full ramp):
- [ ] Collect 48h telemetry summary (latency, errors, cost).
- [ ] Close JIRA JIRA-ENG-1942 with results and link to dashboards.
- [ ] Short retro with on-call + telemetry lead (20m).
- [ ] Archive release artifacts in GCS and tag repo.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- CI artifact: gs://redwood-builds/synapse/1.12.4/synapse-1.12.4.tar.gz
- Canary manifest: github.com/redwood-inference/k8s/patches/synapse-canary-2026-03-16.yaml
- Replay job id: replay-20260316-07

If anything ambiguous: default to abort and inspect. This doc is intentionally concise — keep the slack channel noisy and use explicit abort messages.

-- Ava (release lead)

(Notes: this is a sketch, still need PRI approval and an SRE signoff on the telemetry gating thresholds before Tue deploy.)
